objects: FDR thresholding; adaptive minimaxity; dense signals
assumptions: Asymptotic results of Abramovich et al. (2000)
conclusion: The cited FDR method has adaptive minimaxity with exact constants, while its cited guarantees do not ensure robustness for denser signals.
scope: Author comparison with the rate guarantees of the empirical Bayes method
span: Abramovich, Benjamini, Donoho and Johnstone (2000) show that the false discovery rate approach provides adaptive asymptotic minimaxity at the level of exact constants, as well as the rates of convergence that we demonstrate for the empirical Bayes method. However, their results do not guarantee robustness for denser signals, and there is some evidence of this nonrobustness in the simulations we report in Section 3.

assumptions: Zhang (2004) uses a more restrictive scenario
conclusion: Zhang gives sharper asymptotic adaptation in a more restrictive setting, using more general priors and infinite-order kernel estimation of marginal densities.
span: In a more restrictive scenario than ours, and mainly concentrating on the application to wavelet smoothing, Zhang (2004) provides an asymptot- ically more sharply adaptive empirical Bayes analysis. This analysis uses much more general families of priors than our simple mixtures, and employs nonparametric infinite-order kernel methods to estimate the corresponding marginal densities.
